editorial:
Imagine a world where your online friends are actually your worst enemies. You get thrown into a story that starts with a messy love triangle and a shooting, which sets the stage for something much scarier. Now, eight people who hang out in a chat room similar to old-school MySpace start turning up dead in their own homes. The vibe is very much about that early internet era where everyone felt safe behind a screen, but a killer is using those same connections to find them. It feels like a digital nightmare where you never know who is actually typing on the other side of the chat.

The acting is decent for this kind of movie, and the mystery keeps you guessing about who is behind the screen. While the pacing slows down a bit in the middle, the kills are creative and the tension builds up nicely. If you like low-budget slashers with a tech twist, you will enjoy this one. It is a great pick if you want something creepy but easy to watch.
endingExplained: You find out that the killings were all about revenge for the original shooting. The killer used the chat room to track the victims and toy with them before finishing them off. In the final scenes, the true identity of the murderer is revealed through a series of clues and messages. After a final struggle, the killer is finally stopped, bringing an end to the digital hunting game and closing the loop on the old grudge.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves early 2000s horror and internet mysteries.
